sections.heading: Have these inputs ready
table: A product or service for V1; individual items and shared costs for V2.
Purchases, materials, work, delivery, operating expenses and your target margin.
Your advertising inputs and conversion assumptions. Record which figures are estimates.
Your own funds or loan assumptions, tax settings and planning period.

pages.title: Business Idea Feasibility Calculator | Nomad360
pages.description: Explore the costs, pricing, sales assumptions and funding a business idea needs. Build a free financial scenario before committing money.
pages.h1: Check the financial feasibility of your business idea
pages.eyebrow: From assumptions to a financial scenario
pages.lead: A business idea needs a selling price, a realistic view of costs and enough cash to fund the work. Use your own inputs to explore how these conditions fit together.

sections.heading: Separate evidence from assumptions
paragraphs: A supplier quote can support a purchase cost. A planned number of orders is still an assumption until you have evidence from customers. Keep that distinction when entering your scenario.
table: Supplier quotes, material quantities, work time, delivery and operating expenses.
Advertising budget, cost per click and conversion assumptions appropriate to your route.
A target margin and the tax settings that apply to your scenario.
Available own funds or loan terms, the planning period and the timing supported by the selected model.

sections.heading: Review the conditions together
paragraphs: Start with a product or service in V1. Review the resulting costs, price and financial forecast. For several offerings with shared expenses, use the separate V2 portfolio.
Try a lower sales assumption or a higher cost. Compare the projected profit, cash needs and remaining inventory before deciding which inputs need more evidence.

sections.heading: Test the assumptions with customers
paragraphs: The calculator evaluates the numbers you enter. It does not research demand or predict whether people will buy. Customer conversations and actual selling tests remain separate work.

pages.title: Product & Service Pricing Calculator | Nomad360
pages.description: Prepare direct costs, operating expenses, marketing and target margin to calculate a selling price. Use the free product or service calculation.
pages.h1: Calculate what to charge for a product or service
pages.lead: Start with the costs you pay, then review the selling price alongside marketing, taxes and your target margin. A price based on costs still needs testing with actual customers.

sections.heading: What belongs in your pricing scenario?
table: Choose a product or service. For a product, distinguish manufacturing, resale and dropshipping.
What does delivery of one sale cost?
List purchasing or materials, work, logistics and related expenses supported by your chosen branch.
Identify staff, equipment and operating expenses. For V2, distinguish shared and individual costs.
Enter advertising and conversion assumptions. Do not treat a forecast as confirmed demand.
Review the applicable target margin, taxes and financing settings. Margin and markup are different measures.

sections.heading: Use the branch that matches your work
paragraphs: V1 models one product or service. V2 models several offerings with shared and individual expenses. Use the existing choice in the calculator to select the route that matches your business.

sections.heading: A profitable price can still leave a cash gap
paragraphs: Review payment timing and required funding in the cash-flow calculation. Projected profit and the money available to pay bills answer different questions.

pages.title: Small Business Cash Flow Calculator | Nomad360
pages.description: Review monthly receipts, payments, financing and cash needs using your own assumptions. Model one offering or a V2 portfolio for free.
pages.lead: Projected profit does not tell you whether cash will be available when a payment is due. Review the monthly cash-flow model alongside the costs and sales assumptions behind it.

sections.heading: Prepare the timing assumptions
table: Your chosen route, production or purchasing cycle and sales assumptions.
The receipts, payments and inventory timing supported by the model you select.
How will you fund the work?
Your own funds or the loan principal, interest and term you enter.
The available planning horizon; review the monthly schedule, not only the total.

sections.heading: Use one offering or a portfolio
paragraphs: Complete the V1 costs, marketing and tax steps for one product or service, then use its full cash-flow calculation. For several offerings, V2 models individual and shared costs in a portfolio.
Review expenses that occur before sales, debt payments and unsold inventory. A forecast based on your inputs does not establish future sales.

sections.heading: Read profit and cash separately
paragraphs: Revenue, profit, cash flow and available cash describe different parts of the scenario. Check the monthly schedule and funding needs before assuming that a positive projected profit means every payment can be covered.

pages.h1: A useful financial calculator for your clients
pages.lead: Help visitors prepare better questions about costs, prices and cash needs before a consultation. Explore the existing downloadable calculator for use on your website.

sections.heading: Questions your clients can explore
table: A V1 product or service scenario using costs, marketing assumptions and a target margin.
How much money will I need?
Funding and monthly cash flow, using the assumptions supported by the selected route.
What if I sell several offerings?
A V2 portfolio with individual and shared costs.

sections.heading: Open the existing placement options
paragraphs: The B2B section in the calculator has a button that opens a comparison table. Use “Download free version” to generate the complete HTML file. Preparation and download status appear there, together with a retry link.
The same table contains the existing contact action for a custom version. The free HTML file is provided as the current calculator, with its existing branding and licence terms.

sections.heading: Set expectations for visitors
paragraphs: The calculator does not collect visitor enquiries for your firm or send you their financial scenarios. A useful tool does not guarantee traffic, leads or new clients.

Review the existing data, privacy and licence information before placement. The downloaded edition can still depend on public resources and optional exchange-rate requests; it is not a promise of complete offline operation.
